name: Savanna
notes: Tropical grassland with scattered fire-adapted trees: continuous C4 grass layer under flat-crowned acacias, baobabs and palms. Drawn on the East African Serengeti/miombo, Brazilian Cerrado, Australian tropical savanna and Indian savanna-woodland.

canopy.name: Acacia
canopy.source: Vachellia (Acacia) tortilis, umbrella thorn, flat-topped icon of East African savanna, 4-14 m — Wikipedia / Kew

canopy.name: Baobab
canopy.source: Adansonia digitata, African baobab, scattered giant of sub-Saharan savanna, 8-25 m — Wikipedia

canopy.name: Miombo tree
canopy.source: Brachystegia spiciformis, msasa, dominant of miombo woodland-savanna in southern-central Africa, red spring flush, 10-20 m — Wikipedia / PROTA

canopy.name: Darwin stringybark
canopy.source: Eucalyptus tetrodonta, Darwin stringybark, dominant tree of Australian tropical savanna woodland, 15-30 m — Wikipedia

canopy.name: Cerrado pequi
canopy.source: Caryocar brasiliense, pequi, twisted thick-barked tree typical of Brazilian Cerrado, 6-12 m — Wikipedia

canopy.name: Palmyra palm
canopy.source: Borassus flabellifer, palmyra/toddy palm, fan palm of Indian and SE Asian savanna plains, 15-30 m; B. aethiopum the African equivalent — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Sicklebush
shrub.source: Dichrostachys cinerea, sicklebush, thorny savanna shrub across Africa/India, 2-7 m — Wikipedia / PROTA

shrub.name: Savanna bamboo
shrub.source: Oxytenanthera abyssinica, African lowland/savanna bamboo, clumps in seasonally dry African savanna woodland, 5-12 m — Wikipedia / PROTA

shrub.name: Whistling thorn
shrub.source: Vachellia drepanolobium, whistling thorn, ant-galled acacia forming near-monoculture stands on East African black-cotton savanna, 1.5-6 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Candelabra tree
shrub.source: Euphorbia candelabrum, candelabra tree, succulent spurge on rocky East African savanna, 4-12 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Australian screw pine
shrub.source: Pandanus spiralis, common screw pine, stilt-rooted rosette tree of northern Australian savanna floodplains, 3-10 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Savanna grass
ground.source: Themeda triandra, red oat/kangaroo grass, dominant grass of African, Indian and Australian savanna, 0.3-1.5 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Red grass
ground.source: Hyparrhenia rufa, jaragua/thatching grass, tall dominant of African wet savanna, 1-2.5 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Elephant grass
ground.source: Cenchrus (Pennisetum) purpureus, elephant/napier grass, giant tussocks in moist African savanna and river margins, 2-4 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Spear grass
ground.source: Heteropogon contortus, black spear grass, dominant of Australian and Indian dry savanna, 0.3-1 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Spinifex
ground.source: Triodia pungens, soft spinifex, hummock grass of northern Australian sandy savanna, 0.3-1 m mounds — Wikipedia

ground.name: Fire lily
ground.source: Gloriosa superba, flame lily, tendril-climbing savanna herb across Africa/Asia, 0.5-3 m — Wikipedia
